items.description: The Dja area in southeastern Cameroon is made up of low hills and dense forest terrain. It belongs to the country's southern upland zone.
The Kribi area sits on a gently rising coastal relief. It links the Atlantic lowlands to the inland forest belt.
The Bouba area in the north has broad inland relief with open terrain. It is part of the country’s northern landscape.
The Waza area lies in the dry far north with flat terrain and Sahel conditions. Its relief is shaped by open plains and seasonal watercourses.
The Logone area is part of the low-lying northern plains near the border. It is shaped by floodplains and broad river valleys.
The Kadey area in the east combines rolling terrain and river basins. It belongs to the broader forested upland zone.
The Nyong area is a forested river landscape in southern Cameroon. Its relief is shaped by humid lowlands and drainage basins.
The Sangha area in the southeast is a low forested basin with broad river corridors. It belongs to Cameroon's southern rainforest zone.
